The mission

HGA exists to build grading you can trust: every grade explained, every card housed, and every improvement made in the open, with the hobby and for the hobby.

HGA is owned by uCollect and grades independently, to our published standards. We don't buy, sell or own cards. We grade them.

Every card housed

Built to be kept,
shown and checked.

What we rebuilt

Old problems.
New promises.

Every change is one you can check: on the label, in the report, or in your portal.

Turnaround

A guaranteed date

15 business days from delivery to reveal, or the full price back. Published on time rates per tier, every month.

Housings

Two new cases

HGA Poly, tooled to every card size on the market. HGA Glass, our patented metal and glass housing.

The standard

Published in full

Every grade defined, every threshold in writing, every card graded blind and released by a senior grader.

The record

A report on every card

Every defect located, rated and imaged, tied to an NFT chip in the label. Public on the cert.

The vision · ten years

Trust, cases
and scale.

We're building for the next decade, not the next drop. A grade from HGA should still be worth looking up in 2036.

01

Trust

The strongest database in the hobby

Every grade explained. Every defect a grader identifies is documented, located and rated; every card is imaged. The database grows with every card we grade.

02

Cases

Value beyond the label

Every card housed. HGA Poly for every size on the market; HGA Glass, our metal and glass housing, for premium cards.

03

Scale

Built to keep promises

Every improvement made in the open. Facilities, machines, engineering and people invested ahead of demand, so growth never breaks a promise.

  1. Now to 2027

    Launch it. Prove it.

    All sports and all TCG. Keep every promise we launched with. Listen, and improve in the open.

  2. 2028 to 2030

    Publish and grow

    The database opens to the hobby. Volume grows and turnaround holds. The housing lineup grows with the hobby.

  3. 2031 to 2036

    Set the standard

    The most trusted company in the hobby. The reference for any card, whoever graded it. The case a card should live in.
